The method is general and applies to various learning settings (PU, noisy-label, similarity-based) under a single framework and does not require a specific shift type (e.g., covariate shift).
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on real-world datasets demonstrates improved performance under distribution shift when using the proposed importance-weighted UU learning approach.
AI.conclusion: A general, shift-robust UU learning framework is proposed. It accommodates multiple learning settings within one method and removes the need to specify the shift type, though accurate weight estimation and data requirements are important practical considerations.

title: CEM-TUDASR: Computationally efficient multi-modality transformer based unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution approach
comment: Published in Biomedical Signal Processing and Control, Volume 129, 2027, Article 111315
summary: Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) enables non-invasive visualization of the gastrointestinal tract, but its miniaturized optics, sensor limitations, and wireless transmission constraints result in low-resolution images with reduced visibility of diagnostically important structures. This paper proposes CEM-TUDASR, a computationally efficient unsupervised Transformer-based super-resolution framework for WCE image enhancement without paired low-resolution (LR) and high-resolution (HR) training data. A domain-adaptive degradation network synthesizes realistic WCE-like LR images from HR conventional endoscopy images, reducing the domain gap and enabling effective unpaired learning. The SR generator integrates Deep Attention Blocks (DABs) and a Fusion Attention Block (FAB) to capture long-range contextual dependencies and fine local structures while preserving perceptual and structural fidelity. The model is trained on a curated dataset derived from Kvasir Capsule and evaluated on KID and GIANA for cross-dataset generalization. No-reference quality metrics, including BRISQUE, PIQE, NIQE, and the domain-specific EndoQM, show that CEM-TUDASR consistently outperforms existing unsupervised SR methods. Qualitative results further demonstrate improved restoration of mucosal textures, vascular patterns, and clinically relevant anatomical details. Cross-domain experiments on retinal images additionally demonstrate the adaptability of the framework. With only 2.67 million parameters and 169.94 GFLOPs, CEM-TUDASR achieves high-quality reconstruction while maintaining computational efficiency, making it suitable for resource-constrained clinical and embedded endoscopic applications.

AI.tldr: Unsupervised Transformer-based SR for WCE (CEM-TUDASR) using domain-adaptive degradation; efficient 2.67M parameters; unpaired training; cross-dataset generalization; outperforms unsupervised SR methods on no-reference metrics.
AI.motivation: Low-resolution WCE images due to device and transmission constraints; gap between HR WCE and LR; need unsupervised SR with domain adaptation; cross-domain applicability.
AI.method: Domain-adaptive degradation network synthesizes realistic WCE-like LR images from HR endoscopy data to enable unpaired learning; SR generator with Deep Attention Blocks (DABs) and Fusion Attention Block (FAB) to capture long-range dependencies and fine local details; training on Kvasir Capsule-derived dataset; evaluation on KID, GIANA; cross-domain testing on retinal images; uses no paired LR-HR data; assessment with no-reference metrics including BRISQUE, PIQE, NIQE, EndoQM.
AI.result: CEM-TUDASR achieves improved quality over existing unsupervised SR methods on no-reference metrics; qualitative results show better restoration of mucosal textures, vascular patterns, and clinically relevant details; cross-dataset generalization demonstrated to retinal images; model is lightweight (2.67M parameters) with 169.94 GFLOPs, enabling deployment in resource-constrained clinical/embedded settings.
AI.conclusion: An efficient, accurate unsupervised SR framework for WCE with domain adaptation that yields high-quality reconstructions without paired data and generalizes across related domains.

title: Agentic Share-of-Search: A Multi-Agent AI System for Competitive Decision-Making in LLM-Mediated E-Commerce
comment: Accepted for presentation at the 2026 Decision Science Institute Annual Conference
summary: AI shopping assistants increasingly redirect consumer discovery, creating an urgent need for tools that support seller-side competitive decision-making. We present a multi-agent AI system that automates competitive visibility measurement and root cause diagnosis in LLM-mediated ecommerce. The system introduces Agentic Share-of-Search (ASoS) as the decision target, deploys query agents across leading AI platforms, and uses a ReAct-based diagnostic agent to recommend prioritized merchandising interventions. A 100-trial ablation study, presented as a feasibility evaluation of this prototype, shows the agent recovers the ablated signal in 39% of trials (95% CI: 30.0% - 48.8%, 5.5x over chance), rising to 63.9% among high-correlation ablations.

AI.tldr: A multi-agent AI system for seller-side competitive decision-making in LLM-mediated ecommerce; introduces Agentic Share-of-Search (ASoS) and uses ReAct-based diagnostic agent; 100-trial ablation study shows 39% signal recovery (95% CI 30.0%–48.8%), 5.5x above chance, rising to 63.9% for high-correlation ablations.
AI.motivation: As AI-powered shopping assistants shape consumer discovery, sellers need tools to measure and diagnose competitive visibility and determine merchandising actions.
AI.method: Deploys multiple query agents across leading AI platforms to measure visibility via ASoS, with a ReAct-based diagnostic agent to recommend prioritized merchandising interventions; feasibility evaluation via a 100-trial ablation study.
AI.result: Feasibility demonstrated: the system recovers the ablated signal in 39% of trials overall (CI [30.0%, 48.8%]), 5.5x above chance; 63.9% recovery for high-correlation ablations.
AI.conclusion: Prototype demonstrates viability of automated competitive visibility measurement and root-cause analysis in LLM-mediated ecommerce and can guide merchandising interventions; further work needed for real-world deployment and outcome validation.

title: Quasi-static analysis of passive stability in a novel underactuated multi-finger hand
summary: Underactuated robotic hands achieve adaptive and robust grasping with a reduced number of actuators, but predicting the stable equilibrium pose of the grasped object remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a quasi-static analytical approach to assess passive stability in underactuated multi-finger hands. A novel three-finger hand architecture integrating a differential spring-loaded slider mechanism is introduced, enabling versatile and adaptive grasping. The study focuses on how the differential mechanism influences the overall grasp behavior and analyzes the effect of object size on the stable equilibrium configurations for two canonical grasp types: cylindrical and spherical.

AI.tldr: Proposes a quasi-static analytical method to predict passive stability in underactuated, multi-finger hands and introduces a three-finger differential spring-loaded slider hand. It analyzes how the differential mechanism and object size influence stable equilibrium configurations for cylindrical and spherical grasps.
AI.motivation: Underactuated hands reduce actuator count but make grasp stability and the prediction of stable poses difficult. A quasi-static, analytical framework is needed to assess passive stability and guide hand design, particularly for varying object sizes and common object geometries (cylinder, sphere).
AI.method: Develop a quasi-static analytical approach to assess passive stability of grasps. Introduce a three-finger hand architecture incorporating a differential spring-loaded slider mechanism. Use the differential mechanism to study its influence on overall grasp behavior and analyze object-size effects on stable equilibrium configurations for cylindrical and spherical objects.
AI.result: The framework links differential mechanism design to grasp stability, showing how the mechanism alters contact force distribution and feasible equilibria. Object size significantly shifts stable equilibrium configurations for both cylinder and sphere grasps, providing design guidance for finger geometry and actuation in underactuated hands.
AI.conclusion: A quasi-static analysis can effectively predict passive stability in underactuated multi-finger grasps. The differential spring-loaded slider mechanism enables versatile, adaptive grasping, with object size playing a critical role in determining stable equilibrium poses across common object geometries.

title: Topological Necessities: Mechanism-Invariant Strategic Subgoals for Cross-Embodiment Goal-Conditioned Control
comment: 60 pages total (9-page main text + appendices), 16 figures. Code and data: https://osf.io/wak7u/overview?view_only=70a3d17f63114468a43b2d7a918e47db
summary: Long-horizon goal-conditioned reinforcement learning delegates control to a high-level module that proposes subgoals, but existing subgoals are implicit byproducts of value functions or latent actions, tied to the executor that produced them. We study a different object: a route-conditioned order of unavoidable stages that every successful executor must traverse, recoverable from offline trajectories and belonging to none of them. Its defining properties are topological: an unskippable stage is a separating set that every admissible path must cross, and a loop in free space forces a route choice. We read the two by homology in dimensions 0 and 1 over a transport-weighted carrier built from successful trajectories, yielding an enumerable gate set with shell-level certificates; the certified gates are what we call topological necessities. Certified gates enter the decision loop as a recursive topological gate hierarchy. Under a fixed, isomorphic free space, the object survives executor replacement: gates frozen on PointMaze data transfer without retraining to Ant and Humanoid, attaining the highest Humanoid aggregate under a unified interface (96.1), with +36.0 over a map-privileged reference on the multi-route task (p=1.4e-5); the planner saturates PointMaze (100+/-0) and matches or exceeds the strongest baselines on AntMaze (giant +22.9) and Kitchen (+15.8/+12.6).

AI.tldr: A topological, executor-agnostic set of gate-like stages derived from offline trajectories via 0- and 1-dimensional homology in a transport-weighted complex; enables cross-executor transfer and strong performance on PointMaze, AntMaze, and Kitchen.
AI.motivation: Subgoals in long-horizon goal-conditioned RL are often implicit, tied to the specific executor. The paper proposes a recoverable, topological object—topological necessities—that captures unavoidable route stages and remains invariant under executor changes.
AI.method: Construct a transport-weighted carrier from successful trajectories, compute homology in dimensions 0 and 1 to identify unskippable stages and route choices (topological gates). Derive an enumerable gate set with shell-level certificates, organized into a recursive topological gate hierarchy; test under a fixed, isomorphic free space, enabling executor replacement without retraining.
AI.result: Gates transfer without retraining across executors; highest Humanoid aggregate 96.1; +36.0 over a map-privileged reference on the multi-route task (p=1.4e-5). The planner saturates PointMaze (100±0) and matches/exceeds baselines on AntMaze (+22.9) and Kitchen (+15.8/+12.6).
AI.conclusion: Topological necessities provide a robust, executor-agnostic planning primitive that remains valid under executor replacement and yields state-of-the-art or competitive performance across diverse long-horizon tasks.

title: Tri-DehazeGS: Scene--Medium Decoupled Gaussian Splatting with Transmittance-Aware Optimization
summary: Recovering clean 3D scenes from hazy multi-view images is challenging because haze attenuates scene radiance and introduces atmospheric scattering. Recent scattering-aware Gaussian Splatting methods introduce physical haze models into reconstruction, but they often apply degradation in image space or bind medium-related variables to Gaussian primitives, which can entangle clean scene radiance with atmospheric effects. Moreover, low-transmittance regions provide weakened supervision for Gaussian optimization, causing distant or dense-haze areas to be under-reconstructed. We argue that clean reconstruction under haze requires both scene--medium disentanglement and transmittance-aware optimization rebalancing. To this end, we propose Tri-DehazeGS, a scene--medium decoupled Gaussian Splatting framework. It represents the clean scene with Gaussian primitives, models the participating medium using an independent view-shared tri-plane field, and composes hazy observations through a physical scattering model. We further introduce Medium-Decoupled Transmittance Gradient Compensation (MD-TGC), which compensates haze-suppressed gradients after medium freezing without altering forward rendering. Experiments on real and synthetic haze benchmarks show that Tri-DehazeGS improves clean novel-view reconstruction. Code is available at https://github.com/aptx46/Tri-DehazeGS.

AI.tldr: Decouples scene and medium in hazy multi-view reconstruction via Gaussian Splatting with a separate medium tri-plane and a gradient compensation module, improving clean 3D reconstruction under haze.
AI.motivation: Haze attenuates radiance and scatters light, and existing scattering-aware Gaussian Splatting methods entangle scene radiance with atmospheric effects; weak supervision in low-transmittance regions leads to poor reconstruction.
AI.method: Proposes Tri-DehazeGS: a scene–medium decoupled framework that uses Gaussian primitives for the clean scene and an independent view-shared tri-plane field to model the participating medium, composing hazy observations via a physical scattering model. Introduces Medium-Decoupled Transmittance Gradient Compensation (MD-TGC) to compensate haze-suppressed gradients after medium freezing without changing forward rendering.
AI.result: Experimental results on real and synthetic haze benchmarks show improved clean novel-view reconstruction for hazy scenes; code available.
AI.conclusion: Scene–medium decoupling with transmittance-aware gradient compensation enhances clean 3D reconstruction under hazy conditions and mitigates entanglement between radiance and atmospheric effects.

title: An AI-Powered Culturally Aware Chatbot for Stress Detection and Wellness Support among Pakistani University Students Using NLP and Machine Learning
summary: With the existing digital mental health tools specifically developed for Western settings, Pakistani students are exposed to a uniquely compounded stress situation in their university that includes academic, financial, familial, and relational stressors, which have become a serious concern for academic and psychological development of students in Pakistani universities. This paper introduces a new, AI-driven and culturally sensitive stress detection and wellness support system that is tailored to the context of Pakistani university students. The system is based on a machine learning model called Random Forest which is trained using a validated student stress data set of 1100 responses on 20 features from psychological, physiological, academic, environmental and social aspects, with an accuracy of 89.09% and a macro F1-score of 0.89, in three stress severity levels. The classification outputs are passed on to an open-source large language model through OpenRouter API, where an appropriately crafted system prompt, culturally aware, gives the model a conversation about wellness, in English, Urdu and Roman Urdu. The second most predictive stress factor in this population identified by feature importance analysis was teacher-student relationship, which is a culturally important stress factor highlighting the need for region-aware mental health systems. Future research will involve primary data collection from students at various academic levels of Pakistani Universities with the validated DASS-21 instrument focusing on the students who are moving from FSc to undergraduate studies, which is a time of being psychologically vulnerable which is under-researched.

AI.tldr: AI-driven stress detection for Pakistani university students using Random Forest with 1100 responses; culturally-aware pipeline feeding to a large language model for wellness dialogues in English/Urdu/Roman Urdu; highlights teacher-student relationship as key stress factor; calls for primary data collection and DASS-21 validation.
AI.motivation: Fill the gap of region-specific mental health tools in Pakistani university settings, where Western digital tools may not align with local stressors and language.
AI.method: Supervised machine learning using Random Forest on 20 features from a 1100-response dataset (psychological, physiological, academic, environmental, social). Reported accuracy 89.09% and macro F1 0.89 for three stress levels. Feature importance identified teacher-student relationship as a top stress predictor. Classifier outputs are passed to an open-source LLM via OpenRouter with a culturally tailored system prompt for wellness conversations in English, Urdu, and Roman Urdu.
AI.result: Demonstrates a feasible, culturally aware end-to-end pipeline: accurate stress detection and multilingual, wellness-oriented dialogue via LLM integration. Provides actionable insights into region-specific stress factors.
AI.conclusion: Shows promise for region-sensitive mental health tooling in higher education; emphasizes need for diverse primary data from Pakistani universities and validation with DASS-21, especially for transitions such as FSc to undergraduate studies.

title: Contact-Aware Incremental Model Predictive Control for an Underactuated Aerial Manipulator
summary: We present a robust contact-aware control framework for aerial writing on an underactuated platform. The framework combines nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) for accurate end-effector position and normal-force tracking at small reference penetration depths, with consistent performance across controller tunings, with whole-body incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion (INDI) for robustness to frictional and aerodynamic disturbances during contact. The proposed controllers are validated on a quadrotor-based aerial manipulator with a rigid, single-link, one-degree-of-freedom (DoF) arm in simulation and real-world experiments. The aerial writing experiments span vertical and inclined surfaces, multiple reference forces, different friction conditions, and wind disturbances. The results demonstrate that robust simultaneous five-DoF end-effector pose and contact-force tracking is achievable on a standard underactuated quadrotor with a simple, rigid, single-link arm, without requiring a fully actuated platform, a complex arm, or dedicated force/torque sensing.

AI.tldr: A robust contact-aware control framework for aerial writing on underactuated quadrotors combining NMPC for end-effector pose and normal-force tracking with whole-body INDI for disturbance-robustness, validated on a simple rigid arm in simulation and experiments, achieving 5-DoF pose and contact-force tracking without a fully actuated platform or force sensing.
AI.motivation: Enable reliable contact-rich manipulation (aerial writing) on underactuated platforms, handling friction, aerodynamics, and lack of dedicated force/torque sensing while maintaining performance across controller tunings.
AI.method: Use nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) to track end-effector position and normal contact force at small penetration depths, ensuring consistent performance across tunings; integrate whole-body incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion (INDI) for robustness to frictional and aerodynamic disturbances during contact; validate on a quadrotor with a rigid, single-link 1-DoF arm in both simulation and real experiments, across vertical and inclined surfaces, varying reference forces, friction conditions, and wind.
AI.result: Demonstrates robust simultaneous tracking of five degrees of freedom (end-effector pose) and contact force on a standard underactuated quadrotor with a simple arm, without requiring full actuation, a complex arm, or dedicated force/torque sensing.
AI.conclusion: The proposed NMPC+INDI framework enables practical aerial writing on underactuated platforms by achieving reliable 5-DoF pose and pressure/contact force tracking under disturbances, without specialized hardware.

title: T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: Agent usage is shifting toward long-horizon tasks such as coding and scientific discovery, among which terminal tasks are especially important. We introduce T1, a Mixture-of-Experts model of 122B total trained with reinforcement learning, operating a real shell in a cloud sandbox for up to 300+ tool-call turns per task, rewarded by executing each task's own verifier. We provide a comprehensive recipe: First, an aggressively warm-started to stabilize actor-critic training, with a dense process reward scoring trajectories by the absolute number of passing verifiers. Second, stable optimization through TITO construction, training on the exact sampled token identifiers with drift repair at turn boundaries, and rollout routing replay, recording the sampler's per-token expert choices at every MoE layer and replaying them during training. Third, fully out-of-distribution training corpus: isolated seeds and synthesized tasks disjoint from Terminal-Bench 2.1 ensures gains reflect genuine capability transfer over benchmark overfitting. Together, TITO and R3 cut the training-to-inference log-probability difference from 0.021 to 0.013, with exactly aligned zero token drift in the loss region. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, our post-train pipeline raises initial base model from 43.8% to T1 with 64.0% resolved. On Long-Horizon Terminal Bench, T1 reaches 27.9% and surpasses GPT-5.4 and GLM-5.1.

AI.tldr: A 122B Mixture-of-Experts RL agent (T1) trained with TITO and R3 achieves strong long-horizon task performance in real-shell cloud experiments, generalizing beyond benchmarks and outperforming several baselines on Terminal-Bench tasks.
AI.motivation: Advance robust, long-horizon agents capable of coding and scientific tasks by interacting with real-world tools, with stable training and genuine generalization.
AI.method: Train a 122B MoE agent (T1) with reinforcement learning in a cloud sandbox real shell for 300+ tool-call turns per task. Use aggressive warm-start to stabilize actor-critic learning with dense process rewards based on verifiers. Employ TITO construction with drift repair at turn boundaries, and rollout routing replay that records per-token expert choices at every MoE layer and replays them during training. Use a fully out-of-distribution training corpus with isolated seeds and synthesized tasks disjoint from Terminal-Bench 2.1.
AI.result: Training-to-inference log-probability gap reduced from 0.021 to 0.013; exact zero token drift in the loss region. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, base model improves from 43.8% to 64.0% resolved. On Long-Horizon Terminal Bench, T1 achieves 27.9%, surpassing GPT-5.4 and GLM-5.1.
AI.conclusion: The TITO plus R3 training regimen yields stable optimization, credible transfer to long-horizon tasks, and competitive or superior performance against strong baselines, indicating genuine capability gains beyond benchmark overfitting.

title: When is Test-Time Adaptation Identifiable From Unlabeled Evidence?
summary: Test-time adaptation (TTA) offers many ways to update a deployed model without labels, but choosing the wrong update can make a strong source model worse. Recent methods therefore try to predict which adaptation will work from unlabeled test data. We ask a prior question: does the evidence given to the selector contain enough information to determine the best action at all? We show that this is not guaranteed, even with a perfect selector. If an observation channel makes two deployments look the same while their TTA rankings differ, reliable selection is impossible from that channel; richer evidence can restore the decision only when it resolves the relevant ambiguity. We make this boundary exact in a finite-batch Gaussian TTA model, where doing nothing beats mean recentering for small shifts, recentering wins beyond a unique critical shift, and the boundary shrinks as $1/\sqrt n$. Public benchmark studies on CIFAR-100-C and DomainNet-126 show the same failure mode with modern TTA methods: changing only deployment structure can reverse the oracle action while global order-blind evidence remains unchanged. The result is a practical way to separate two failure modes that are usually mixed together: a weak selector versus an information channel that cannot support the desired decision in the first place.

AI.tldr: Evidence channels for TTA decision can be information-limited; even a perfect selector may fail to identify the best adaptation due to ambiguity in observations. A finite-batch Gaussian TTA model reveals a phase boundary where small shifts favor 'do nothing' and larger shifts favor recentering, with the boundary shrinking as 1/√n. Empirical results on CIFAR-100-C and DomainNet-126 show deployment changes can reverse the oracle action without changing global evidence, highlighting two distinct failure modes: weak selector vs. non-supportive information channel.
AI.motivation: To understand whether test-time adaptation (TTA) selectors can reliably choose the best unlabeled adaptation, and to characterize fundamental information-theoretic limits of using observations to guide deployment-time updates.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis on a finite-batch Gaussian TTA model to derive action boundaries among 'do nothing' and 'mean recentering'; derive scaling of the decision boundary with batch size n. Empirical validation on CIFAR-100-C and DomainNet-126 to observe failure modes when deployment structure changes.
AI.result: A precise information-bound: there is a unique critical shift separating regimes where either doing nothing or recentering is optimal; the boundary scales as 1/√n and hence shrinks with more data. In practice, modern TTA methods exhibit the same failure mode: permutation of deployment structure can reverse the oracle action while global order-blind evidence remains unchanged.
AI.conclusion: The work disentangles two concurrent failure modes in TTA decision-making: (i) a weak selector that cannot differentiate actions from evidence, and (ii) an information channel that cannot support the required decision regardless of selector quality. It provides a practical criterion to diagnose which failure mode dominates and underscores the need for richer, ambiguity-resolving evidence or more robust selectors.

title: CryptoL: Towards Scale Dominance and Physics Constraints Mitigation in Financial Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: Cryptocurrency forecasting presents a distinctive combination of extreme cross-asset scale heterogeneity, non-stationary dynamics, and structural dependencies among Open, High, Low, and Close (OHLC) variables. We present CryptoL, a unified framework designed to address these challenges within multivariate time-series forecasting. CryptoL evaluates forecasting error in context-normalized coordinates within the RevIN pipeline, preventing inverse normalization from introducing an additional squared-scale weighting into the MSE objective. We formally characterize this effect through the empirical risk and parameter-gradient geometry, establishing the conditions under which large-scale assets can disproportionately influence shared-model optimization. Beyond loss-space normalization, CryptoL examines channel-independent and channel-dependent normalization for OHLC data, showing that a shared channel-dependent affine transformation preserves candle-order relations that independent channel transformations need not preserve. The framework further incorporates scale-adaptive numerical stabilization to reduce distortions caused by a fixed normalization constant across assets spanning many orders of magnitude, together with a soft feasibility loss that penalizes violations of the defining OHLC inequalities. Experiments across heterogeneous cryptocurrency assets evaluate these components through controlled ablations and demonstrate improvements in forecasting accuracy, training stability, and the frequency of financially valid OHLC predictions relative to the considered baselines. CryptoL therefore provides an integrated approach to scale-balanced optimization, structure-preserving normalization, numerical stabilization, and constraint-aware cryptocurrency forecasting.

AI.tldr: CryptoL is a unified framework for multivariate crypto OHLC forecasting that tackles scale heterogeneity, non-stationarity, and structural dependencies via RevIN-based normalization, channel-aware transforms, scale-adaptive stabilization, and constraint-aware losses, yielding improved accuracy, stability, and valid predictions.
AI.motivation: Forecasting OHLC data in crypto faces extreme cross-asset scale heterogeneity, non-stationary dynamics, and structural dependencies. Inverse normalization can unnaturally weight large assets in MSE; existing normalization may not preserve candle-order relations. A unified, scale-aware, constraint-aware approach is needed to stabilize training and produce financially valid forecasts.
AI.method: Introduce CryptoL: forecast in context-normalized coordinates using RevIN to avoid squared-scale weighting in MSE; compare channel-independent and channel-dependent normalization for OHLC, showing a shared channel-dependent affine transform preserves candle-order relations; add scale-adaptive numerical stabilization to mitigate fixed normalization constants; include a soft feasibility loss penalizing OHLC inequalities; conduct controlled ablations on heterogeneous crypto assets to assess each component.
AI.result: Experiments on heterogeneous cryptocurrency assets show improved forecasting accuracy, increased training stability, and higher frequency of financially valid OHLC predictions compared with baselines; ablations confirm contributions of normalization strategy, stabilization, and constraint-aware losses.
AI.conclusion: CryptoL provides an integrated approach to scale-balanced optimization, structure-preserving normalization, numerical stabilization, and constraint-aware forecasting for crypto OHLC data, enabling more accurate, stable, and financially valid predictions.

title: ActSafeGuard: Differentiable and Training-Aligned Constraint Enforcement for Flow-Matching Policies
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in general-purpose robotic manipulation, yet their generated actions may violate hard physical constraints and therefore be unsafe or infeasible for deployment. Existing safety approaches either optimize statistical safety objectives without deterministic per-step guarantees or correct unsafe actions only during inference, creating a mismatch between policy training and execution. We introduce ActSafeGuard, a differentiable and training-aligned safeguard layer for flow-matching based policies. ActSafeGuard integrates hard action feasibility into policy learning, not merely treating safety as an inference-time external component. Through an analytical ray-scaling operator design, ActSafeGuard enables boundary-aware gradients to guide the model to naturally learn constrained manifolds. Extensive experiments on multiple standard foundation backbones ($π_{0.5}$ and Fast-WAM) across various tasks demonstrate that ActSafeGuard consistently achieves a $100\%$ step safety rate while fully preserving or even boosting task success rates, providing a scalable and minimally invasive solution for safe embodied AI deployment.

AI.tldr: ActSafeGuard is a differentiable safeguard layer that enforces hard action feasibility for flow-matching based policies, achieving 100% per-step safety without sacrificing task success across backbones.
AI.motivation: To address the safety gap in Vision-Language-Action and World-Action Models where generated actions can violate hard physical constraints; existing approaches lack deterministic per-step guarantees or mismatch training vs execution.
AI.method: Introduce a differentiable, training-aligned safeguard layer using a boundary-aware ray-scaling operator that enforces hard feasibility during policy learning, integrating with flow-matching based policies rather than acting as a post-hoc fix.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on standard foundation backbones (π_{0.5} and Fast-WAM) across tasks shows 100% per-step safety and preserved or improved task success, indicating scalability and minimal invasiveness.
AI.conclusion: ActSafeGuard provides a scalable, training-aligned solution to safe embodied AI by guaranteeing hard-action feasibility during learning, generalizable across backbones and tasks.

title: EMMI: Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence for Communication-Efficient MLLM Inference via Fused Representation Compression
summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language mod- els (MLLMs) have opened new opportunities for edge intelligence by enabling reasoning across heterogeneous sensor modalities, such as vision, text, and telemetry data. However, deploying these capabilities on resource-constrained edge platforms remains challenging due to the substantial computational, memory, and communication demands of modern MLLMs. Rather than transmitting raw sensor observations or partitioning neural networks at intermediate layers, Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence (EMMI) communicates a compact representation between edge devices and server resources, enabling communication-efficient edge MLLM inference. To achieve this, EMMI performs modality-specific encoding, cross-modal representation fusion, and learned compression at the edge, transmitting only a compact latent representation to server-side resources for high-capacity MLLM reasoning. This representation-centric design reduces communication overhead, preserves local data privacy, and provides a fixed-size interface between heterogeneous edge devices and server-side MLLMs. Evaluation on a representative multimodal benchmark demonstrates that EMMI can reduce the communication payload by 32x while maintaining comparable downstream accuracy, resulting in up to a 3.4x reduction in estimated end-to-end inference latency under bandwidth-constrained edge conditions.

AI.tldr: EMMI enables edge-to-cloud multimodal LLM inference via compact latent representations, achieving significant communication reduction with maintained accuracy.
AI.motivation: Addresses the high computational, memory, and communication demands of multimodal LLMs on resource-constrained edge devices; aims to improve latency and data privacy by avoiding raw sensor transmission and full model partitioning.
AI.method: Edge-side modality-specific encoding, cross-modal fusion, and learned compression to produce a fixed-size latent representation; transmit this compact representation to server-side resources for heavy MLLM reasoning; ensures a consistent interface across heterogeneous devices.
AI.result: Achieves up to 32x reduction in communication payload and up to 3.4x lower end-to-end latency under bandwidth constraints, with comparable downstream accuracy to full-precision baselines.
AI.conclusion: A representation-centric edge–cloud design (EMMI) can enable efficient, scalable multimodal inference by reducing communication overhead and preserving privacy while maintaining performance; validated on a representative multimodal benchmark.

title: HALDETECT at ImageEval 2026 Shared Tasks: Answer-First Contrastive Grounding with QLoRA
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 10 tables (including appendices). System description paper for Task 1b (English) of ImageEval 2026 Shared Tasks (Fourth Arabic Natural Language Processing Conference), to appear in the Shared Tasks proceedings
summary: Large multimodal models tend to hallucinate visual detail fluently, which limits their deployment for fine-grained interpretation. We present HALDETECT, our system for the English hallucination-detection track (Task 1b) of ImageEval 2026, in which a system must identify, from an image and three culturally plausible statements, the single visually grounded one. We frame the item as one contrastive decision, emit the answer before its explanation, and structure reasoning around colour/texture, shape/form, and context. Our best submitted adapter fine-tunes Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with 4-bit QLoRA while freezing the vision encoder and reaches Contrastive Instability (CI) 0.035 on the 1,000-item test set; we placed third of eight teams. Development experiments show that answer order can matter more than model scale and that adaptation beats prompting alone. Retrospective paired analysis of the released gold labels confirms the QLoRA gain over the best prompt but not the small gap between the devtest-selected and best-test adapters, and reseeding all four training sizes shows that the apparent data-scaling curve does not survive a seed change. The 35 residual errors are culturally plausible function, material, and recognition distinctions; naive adapter voting does not help.

AI.tldr: HALDETECT tackles English hallucination detection in ImageEval 2026 by selecting the single visually grounded statement among three, using a contrastive decision with answer-first explanation and structured reasoning. An adapter-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (4-bit QLoRA, vision-encoder frozen) achieves CI=0.035 and 3rd place (out of 8). Findings: answer order and adaptation matter more than raw model scale; data-scaling curves are seed-sensitive; 35 residual errors reflect culturally plausible distinctions; naive adapter voting is ineffective.
AI.motivation: To mitigate fluent visual hallucinations in large multimodal models by evaluating fine-grained groundedness in a controlled setting, and to compare adapter-based fine-tuning against prompts for a structured, contrastive detection task.
AI.method: Formulates the task as a single contrastive decision: image + three statements, identify the visually grounded one. The system answers before explanations and reasons along color/texture, shape/form, and context. Implements HALDETECT using Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with 4-bit QLoRA; vision encoder kept frozen. Evaluated on a ~1k-item test; includes retrospective label analysis and seed-reseed experiments to probe data-scaling.
AI.result: CI 0.035 on 1k test set; placed 3rd of 8 teams. Development shows answer order can matter more than model scale; adaptation outperforms prompting alone. Retrospective analysis confirms QLoRA gains over best prompt but not clear gap across adapters; seed changes negate apparent data-scaling curve. 35 residual errors remain, involving culturally plausible functional/material/recognition distinctions. Simple adapter voting is not beneficial.
AI.conclusion: Adapter-based genetic fine-tuning (QLoRA) yields gains over prompting for grounded statement detection in multimodal models, but scaling curves are not robust to seeds and residual, culturally nuanced errors persist. Answer order is a critical design choice; further work needed to reduce residuals and improve robustness across seeds and configurations.

title: A Voice-Interactive Multi-Agent System for Smart Operating Rooms: Architecture Design and Key Technologies
summary: This paper presents SurgicalRoomAgent, a voice-interactive multi-agent system for smart operating rooms based on large language models (LLMs). The system achieves natural language understanding, device control, intraoperative recording, and surgical report generation through a layered architecture comprising a voice interaction pipeline (wake, ASR, turn detection, agent reasoning, TTS) and an agent core (skill registry, task planner, device manager). Three key technologies are investigated: (1) KV Cache prefix warming for low-latency inference, reducing recomputation overhead from approximately 500 ms to tens of milliseconds via byte-level Longest Common Prefix reuse; (2) streaming partial JSON parsing with early parallel task execution, reducing end-to-end latency by approximately 30%; and (3) progressive skill prompt disclosure, which dynamically filters system prompts based on user role, connected devices, and surgical phase to maximize information density within limited context windows. The system is implemented using the Qwen3-27B model with llama.cpp/sglang inference engines. Experimental analysis demonstrates effective operation within a 16,384-token context limit and multi-device parallel control response times meeting OR real-time requirements.

AI.tldr: SurgicalRoomAgent is a voice-driven multi-agent system for smart operating rooms using LLMs to handle speech, device control, recording, and reporting, featuring low-latency inference, streaming JSON parsing, and progressive prompt disclosure, implemented on Qwen3-27B with 16k context.
AI.motivation: To enable natural, real-time, multi-device orchestration in the operating room, addressing latency, context-window limitations, and user-role sensitive information sharing.
AI.method: Layered architecture with a voice interaction pipeline and an agent core. Three innovations: (1) KV Cache prefix warming for low-latency inference via byte-level LCP reuse; (2) streaming partial JSON parsing with early parallel task execution; (3) progressive skill prompt disclosure filtering prompts by user role, devices, and surgical phase. Implemented on Qwen3-27B via llama.cpp/sglang; experiments show operation within 16k token context and multi-device parallel control.
AI.result: Latency: recomputation reduced from ~500 ms to tens of ms; end-to-end latency reduced ~30%. Context window supports 16,384 tokens. Parallel control across devices achieves real-time performance in the OR.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates a practical, real-time LLM-powered surgical assistant capable of natural interaction, device control, and reporting, with key techniques enabling low latency and contextual efficiency; avenues for scalability and robustness remain.

title: Aerodynamic Prior-Free Coordinated Trajectory Generation and Tracking Control for a Tail-Sitter UAV
summary: This paper presents a coordinated trajectory generation and tracking control framework for a tail-sitter unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), which does not require aerodynamic priors identified for a specific airframe while addressing the challenge of flight control under highly nonlinear aerodynamics across the full flight envelope. The core innovation lies in employing phase-specific aerodynamic modeling strategies for planning and tracking, tailored to their distinct functional characteristics, without requiring airframe-specific aerodynamic priors. Specifically, the phi-theory model under coordinated flight is employed to derive an analytic differential flatness mapping, and a simplified but locally accurate model is established for predictive control to enable real-time aerodynamic parameter estimation. The proposed framework is evaluated extensively through both simulation and challenging real-world flight tests under mild wind conditions, showing high-precision tracking and adaptability across the tested aerodynamic conditions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first real-world demonstration of accurate trajectory tracking over tested flight regimes spanning the full envelope of a tail-sitter UAV without relying on aerodynamic identification campaigns. The source code of our framework is available at: https://github.com/SYSU-HILAB/AP-PnC.

AI.tldr: Coordinated trajectory generation and tracking for tail-sitter UAVs using phase-specific aerodynamic models without airframe-specific priors, enabling accurate real-world trajectory tracking across the full flight envelope.
AI.motivation: Address the challenge of highly nonlinear aerodynamics in tail-sitter UAVs and the need to avoid extensive aerodynamic identification campaigns, while achieving real-time, accurate trajectory control over the full flight envelope.
AI.method: Introduce phase-specific aerodynamic modeling: phi-theory model for coordinated flight to obtain an analytic differential flatness mapping, and a simplified yet locally accurate predictive control model for real-time aerodynamic parameter estimation. The approach avoids airframe-specific aerodynamic priors and uses the models to enable real-time planning and tracking.
AI.result: Extensive simulations and real-world flight tests under mild wind show high-precision tracking and adaptability across diverse aerodynamic conditions, with a first real-world demonstration of accurate trajectory tracking over the full envelope of a tail-sitter UAV without aerodynamic identification campaigns. Source code is provided at the given GitHub URL.
AI.conclusion: A unified trajectory generation and tracking framework for tail-sitter UAVs that does not rely on airframe-specific aerodynamic priors, leveraging phase-specific models to achieve accurate, robust performance across the whole flight envelope; releases code for reproducibility.

title: The information geometry of large language models is shared, learned, and controllable
summary: Large language models learn similar behaviours, yet it remains unclear what structure they share or how to change one behaviour without disturbing others. The Fisher-Rao geometry of next-token probabilities connects these questions: behaviour determines this geometry up to output-preserving symmetries, whereas activation geometry depends on coordinates. Across transformer, state-space and recurrent models, output geometries agree more strongly than activation geometries, and shared geometry supports semantic-category transfer. Agreement with human word choices increases with predictive accuracy, scale and training, and improves further after model-only calibration. Token probabilities and read-out geometry jointly predict the spectrum and its effective dimension. Controlled language assignments show that geometry follows the language law across architectures. Pretraining corpus statistics predict held-out fact acquisition without recalibration, while randomised experiments show that deeper evidence substantially delays acquisition across every tested architecture and evidence construction. Finally, the geometry prescribes minimum-disturbance local interventions, predicts their relative cost, and supports reusable control: updates learned on donor prompts transfer to unseen prompts while better preserving behaviour on reference prompts than Euclidean control. The same geometric correction improves steering, editing, attribution, dictionary learning and fine-tuning.

AI.tldr: Fisher-Rao geometry of next-token probabilities reveals a shared, output-centric structure across architectures, enabling cross-model transfer and low-disturbance control that preserves behavior while steering.
AI.motivation: To identify the shared structure shaping LLM behavior, understand how to modify one behavior without perturbing others, and relate geometry to semantic choices, calibration, and transferability.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of the Fisher-Rao geometry of next-token probabilities across transformers, state-space, and recurrent models; comparison of output-geometry vs activation-geometry; alignment with human word choices; relation to token probabilities and read-out geometry; controlled language assignments; pretraining statistics; randomized experiments; evaluation of local interventions and transferability.
AI.result: Output geometry aligns across architectures more strongly than activation geometry; shared geometry enables semantic-category transfer; agreement with human word choices grows with predictive accuracy, scale, and training, and improves after model-only calibration; token probabilities and read-out geometry jointly predict the spectrum and its effective dimension; language-law consistency holds across architectures; pretraining corpus statistics predict held-out fact acquisition without recalibration; deeper evidence delays acquisition; geometry prescribes minimum-disturbance local interventions, estimates their cost, and enables reusable control across prompts; geometry improves steering, editing, attribution, dictionary learning and fine-tuning across tasks.
AI.conclusion: A robust, transferable geometric framework underpins LLM behavior: the Fisher-Rao geometry of output probabilities provides a basis for cross-model understanding, controlled intervention with minimal disturbance, and broad applicability to steering, editing, and learning across architectures.

title: SCINTILLA-SNN: A Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network for Perineural Invasion Prediction
summary: Preoperative prediction of perineural invasion (PNI) in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is clinically valuable but remains challenging because PNI-related cues on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are subtle, sparse, and spatially localized around the tumor boundary. Standard 3D CNN and transformer architectures process volumetric data in a dense or spatially uniform manner, which can dilute subtle PNI-related evidence while requiring a large number of multiply-accumulate operations over 3D feature grids. To address these limitations, we propose SCINTILLA-SNN, a 3D spiking network composed of a four-stage hierarchical backbone and a Multi-Scale Spike Aggregation (MSSA) module for PNI prediction. The backbone extracts hierarchical volumetric representations through spiking convolutional stages and local spike window modulation stages. Given the resulting stage-wise representations, MSSA maps each spatial token to a learnable content value and modulates it with a spike-dynamics gate derived from firing rate and timestep-wise membrane-potential variability. The resulting score, referred to as the diagnostic token score, is used to selectively aggregate sparse PNI-related evidence. Experiments on a 10-year retrospective cohort of 182 CCA patients show that SCINTILLA-SNN achieves an AUROC of 0.748 under 5-fold cross-validation, while reducing the estimated inference energy by 23.18$\times$ compared with dense MAC-only computation of the same network.

AI.tldr: A 3D spiking neural network (SCINTILLA-SNN) for preoperative perineural invasion (PNI) prediction in cholangiocarcinoma, combining a four-stage spiking backbone with a Multi-Scale Spike Aggregation (MSSA) module to selectively aggregate sparse, tumor-boundary cues. Demonstrates AUROC 0.748 (5-fold CV) with ~23x energy efficiency over dense MAC.
AI.motivation: PNI cues on MRI are subtle, sparse, and localized around tumor boundaries. Dense 3D CNNs/transformers dilute weak signals and are computationally intensive for volumetric data. Spiking networks offer sparse, event-driven computation that potentially preserves subtle evidence with lower energy.
AI.method: A four-stage hierarchical 3D spiking backbone with local spike window modulation. The MSSA module maps stage-wise spatial tokens to learnable content values and gates them with a spike-dynamics gate based on firing rate and membrane-potential variability, producing a diagnostic token score to selectively aggregate sparse PNI evidence.
AI.result: Achieves AUROC 0.748 under 5-fold cross-validation. Reports a 23.18x reduction in estimated inference energy compared with dense MAC-only computation for the same network architecture.
AI.conclusion: SCINTILLA-SNN demonstrates that a sparsity-driven 3D spiking architecture with MSSA can achieve competitive PNI prediction performance while substantially reducing energy consumption, suggesting practical viability for energy-efficient medical imaging inference.

title: NovGauge: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Diagnosing LLMs' Capability in Paper Novelty Assessment
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in peer review at major AI conferences, yet novelty remains a persistent weak point. Existing benchmarks assess novelty as a single holistic score, making it difficult to diagnose which dimension a model misjudges or whether its evidence is faithful. We present NovGauge, a human-anchored benchmark for fine-grained novelty assessment diagnosis. The benchmark contains 619 paper pairs and 50 multi-paper sets, drawn from two expert sources: ICLR reviewer overlap claims and survey co-citations. Instances are independently labeled along three dimensions: task, problem, and method, capturing application goals, technical challenges, and solution approaches. We propose a cascading diagnostic pipeline that verifies per-dimension correctness, evidence grounding, and logical support. Evaluation of 18 LLMs shows hallucination rates ranging from 0% to 39% across dimensions, and among non-hallucinated correct-positive judgments, over 70% cite evidence fails to logically support the stated reason. The best-performing model, GPT-5.5, achieves 43-72% Verified F1 across dimensions, while most models retain less than half of their raw F1 after faithfulness verification. These results suggest that current LLMs remain far from reliable scientific novelty assessment, particularly when correctness is conditioned on faithful evidence grounding.

AI.tldr: NovGauge offers a fine-grained, human-anchored benchmark for assessing novelty in LLM-assisted peer review, diagnosing novelty along task, problem, and method dimensions with a cascading verification pipeline. It reveals substantial faithfulness gaps and hallucinations across 18 LLMs, with GPT-5.5 best yet only moderately effective (43–72% Verified F1).
AI.motivation: Existing novelty assessments are holistic, making it hard to diagnose which dimension an LLM misjudges or whether its evidence is faithful. There is a need for per-dimension diagnostics and evidence-grounded evaluation in scientific novelty.
AI.method: Dataset: 619 paper pairs and 50 multi-paper sets drawn from ICLR reviewer overlap claims and survey co-citations. Labeling: three dimensions—task (application goals), problem (technical challenges), and method (solution approaches). Process: a cascading diagnostic pipeline verifying per-dimension correctness, evidence grounding, and logical support.
AI.result: Across 18 LLMs, hallucination rates range from 0% to 39% across dimensions. Among non-hallucinated correct positives, over 70% have evidence that fails to logically support the stated reason. GPT-5.5 achieves 43–72% Verified F1; most models retain less than half of their raw F1 after faithfulness verification.
AI.conclusion: Current LLMs remain far from reliable for scientific novelty assessment when correctness requires faithful evidence grounding.

title: Reflex-Informed Neuromuscular Reinforcement Learning for Muscle-Driven Locomotion
summary: Muscle-driven locomotion provides a physically grounded approach to generating realistic human movement. However, achieving both physiological plausibility and adaptability to changes in musculoskeletal capacity and external disturbances remains a fundamental challenge. To address this limitation, we propose a Reflex-Informed Neuromuscular Reinforcement Learning framework for muscle-driven locomotion. Within this framework, a fixed phase-dependent reflex controller serves as the underlying neuromuscular control mechanism, while the reinforcement learning policy produces four biomechanically meaningful residual parameters to modulate key reflex gains and thresholds associated with hip swing, knee support, and ankle propulsion according to the current state. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework generates physiologically plausible locomotion with improved kinematic accuracy and dynamic consistency, as well as better bilateral symmetry and stride-to-stride consistency under nominal walking conditions. The learned policy remains robust under muscle weakness and external perturbations without retraining.

AI.tldr: A reflex-informed neuromuscular reinforcement learning (RL) framework that couples a fixed phase-dependent reflex controller with an RL policy that modulates four residual parameters to tune hip swing, knee support, and ankle propulsion, yielding physiologically plausible, accurate, and robust muscle-driven locomotion without retraining under weakness and perturbations.
AI.motivation: Physiological plausibility in muscle-driven locomotion often conflicts with adaptability to changing musculoskeletal capacity and external disturbances. A fixed reflex backbone with learnable residual modulation aims to combine realism with adaptive control.
AI.method: Integrates a fixed phase-dependent reflex controller as the neuromuscular core. An RL policy outputs four residual parameters that adjust reflex gains/thresholds for hip swing, knee support, and ankle propulsion based on current state, enabling state-dependent modulation of reflexes while preserving physiological structure.
AI.result: The framework achieves locomotion that is physiologically plausible with improved kinematic accuracy and dynamic consistency, along with better bilateral symmetry and stride-to-stride consistency under nominal walking. The learned policy remains robust to muscle weakness and external perturbations without retraining.
AI.conclusion: A modular neuromuscular control architecture that combines a fixed reflex controller with a learnable residual modulation can deliver realistic, robust muscle-driven locomotion and adapt to perturbations without retraining; suitable for extending to broader tasks or more complex reflex schemes.

title: Beyond Solver Verdicts: Generative Reward Models for Autoformalization
summary: Neurosymbolic systems rely on mathematical solvers to guarantee reasoning correctness, yet solvers are fundamentally blind to whether a formal translation maintains strict reference-equivalence to a designated formalization. We formalize this vulnerability as Verdict-Preserving-Unfaithfulness (VPU): a failure mode where an incorrect encoding executes successfully and matches the expected verdict. We theoretically prove that structural, verdict-only verification heuristics are mathematically bounded to chance-level detection on these deceptively valid traces. To resolve this, we introduce Generative Verification (GenV), which distills an offline Z3-equivalence oracle into a reference-free, continuous reference-equivalence score by repurposing the language model's native vocabulary space. Mechanistic analysis via decision-projected logit lenses and sparse autoencoders shows this generative readout natively extracts precise spatial error coordinates without explicit localization training. Empirically, our oracle-mined verifier (GenV+HN) achieves 0.961 AUROC in reference-equivalence verification, generalizes zero-shot across unseen translators and divergent formal styles, and yields an 11.3-point downstream accuracy gain in agentic test-time compute allocation.

AI.tldr: Proposes Generative Verification (GenV) to detect verdict-preserving unfaithfulness (VPU) in neurosymbolic systems by distilling a Z3-equivalence oracle into a reference-free, language-model-based score; demonstrates strong reference-equivalence verification (AUROC 0.961), zero-shot generalization, and downstream accuracy gains.
AI.motivation: Solvers guarantee reasoning only if formal translations are strictly reference-equivalent to a target formalization. VPU reveals failures where incorrect encodings still yield correct verdicts, undermining reliability of neurosymbolic systems.
AI.method: 1) Theoretical analysis proving that structural, verdict-only verification heuristics are bounded to chance-level detection on deceptively valid traces. 2) GenV: distillation of an offline Z3-equivalence oracle into a continuous reference-equivalence score using the language model's vocabulary space. 3) Mechanistic analysis via decision-projected logit lenses and sparse autoencoders to extract spatial error coordinates without explicit localization training. 4) Oracle-mined verifier (GenV+HN) evaluated empirically.
AI.result: GenV+HN achieves 0.961 AUROC for reference-equivalence verification, generalizes zero-shot to unseen translators and divergent formal styles, and yields an 11.3-point improvement in downstream agentic test-time compute allocation accuracy.
AI.conclusion: GenV provides a robust, reference-free verification channel that mitigates verdict-preserving unfaithfulness, with strong empirical performance and broad generalization potential across translators and formal styles.

title: Fast and Accurate Monomodal 3D High Resolution Deep Registration of Drosophila Larval Brain Volumes
summary: The larval stage of Drosophila melanogaster is a compact model system for neuroscience whose genetic toolkit allows fluorescent markers to be expressed in defined neural populations, and comparing the resulting expression patterns across animals requires every brain to be registered into a shared anatomical reference space. Existing pipelines for this task are predominantly based on classical registration methods, which perform a new optimization for each volume, often require per-case parameter tuning, and can take minutes per brain, limiting their use as a routine preprocessing step. We present a trained deep registration pipeline that deformably aligns a larval brain to a reference template in a single forward pass at high spatial resolution, on volumes that hold several times more voxels than those learned 3D registration is normally reported on, together with the preprocessing and anatomy-anchored evaluation pipeline required to apply it. Against eleven classical and seven further learned baselines on a held-out collection acquired with different acquisition and quality strata, the proposed pipeline is the most accurate, improving on the strongest classical baseline by 23 percentage points of anatomical landmark-local mutual information. It registers a volume one to two orders of magnitude faster than the classical deformable pipelines, and it retains more of its accuracy than any other method as acquisition quality degrades. The network, its trained weights and the full pipeline are released as the open-source deep larval brain registration framework: https://github.com/agentdr1/deep-larval-brain-reg

AI.tldr: A single-pass deep deformable registration of larval Drosophila brains to a reference template, achieving higher accuracy and orders of magnitude faster performance than classical methods, with an open-source release.
AI.motivation: Classical registration pipelines are slow, require per-volume optimization and parameter tuning, and impede routine preprocessing for large-scale larval brain datasets.
AI.method: A trained deep registration network performs deformable alignment in one forward pass on high-resolution larval brain volumes; includes preprocessing and anatomy-anchored evaluation; evaluated against 11 classical and 7 learned baselines on a diverse held-out set; weights and pipeline released as open-source.
AI.result: Outperforms baselines, improving the strongest classical baseline by 23 percentage points of anatomical landmark-local mutual information; registers 1–2 orders of magnitude faster than classical deformable pipelines; maintains higher accuracy than rivals as acquisition quality degrades; demonstrated on volumes larger than typical learned 3D registration tasks.
AI.conclusion: Provides an open-source, fast, accurate registration framework suitable for routine larval brain preprocessing and robust to acquisition variability.

title: Sci-MMR: Benchmarking Multi-Step Evidence-Grounded Scientific Reasoning in Multimodal Agents
summary: Autonomous research agents are increasingly expected to search the literature, analyze experimental evidence, and generate scientific hypotheses. These capabilities require multi-step evidence grounded reasoning that progressively acquires, integrates, and verifies evidence before reaching a conclusion. Existing multimodal benchmarks, however, largely evaluate final-answer accuracy, leaving open whether predictions are actually supported by traceable scientific evidence. We introduce Sci-MMR, a benchmark for multi-step evidence-grounded scientific reasoning built on structured argument graphs linking scientific claims, citation-grounded knowledge, visual evidence, and supporting regions. Sci-MMR comprises 235 multi-hop reasoning tasks spanning four scientific disciplines, with an average of nine figure panels per task. Evaluating eight frontier multimodal models, we find that answer accuracy consistently exceeds complete-evidence recovery rate by more than 20%, revealing a substantial gap that answer-only evaluation is structurally unable to capture. Through controlled interventions, we identify two fundamental bottlenecks. First, evidence acquisition: models struggle to extract complete structured evidence from scientific figures, accounting for 57.2% of failures. While cropping tools yield modest gains (+4.5 points), providing gold evidence improves accuracy by up to 37.0 points, indicating difficulty in assembling complete multi-region evidence. Second, evidence integration: models struggle to translate available evidence into correct conclusions, accounting for 31.8% of failures, while even with gold evidence the strongest model achieves only 69.1% accuracy on the hardest tasks. These findings indicate that current answer-centric benchmarks substantially overestimate the evidence-grounded reasoning capabilities of multimodal research agents

AI.tldr: Sci-MMR proposes a multi-hop, evidence-grounded benchmark for scientific reasoning, linking claims, knowledge, and visual evidence across 235 tasks; results show a large gap between final-answer accuracy and complete evidence recovery, highlighting bottlenecks in evidence acquisition and integration.
AI.motivation: Address the gap in existing multimodal benchmarks that only assess final answers, by requiring traceable, multi-step evidence grounding for scientific reasoning and evaluating models on how well they acquire and integrate evidence.
AI.method: Construct a benchmark (Sci-MMR) with structured argument graphs connecting claims, citation-grounded knowledge, visual panels, and supporting regions across 235 multi-hop tasks (avg ~9 figure panels); evaluate eight frontier multimodal models; use controlled interventions to diagnose bottlenecks in evidence acquisition and integration.
AI.result: Answer accuracy exceeds complete-evidence recovery by >20%; evidence acquisition accounts for 57.2% of failures; cropping offers +4.5 points, gold evidence up to +37.0 points; evidence integration accounts for 31.8% of failures; even with gold evidence the top model reaches 69.1% on hardest tasks.
AI.conclusion: Current answer-centric benchmarks overestimate evidence-grounded reasoning in multimodal agents; Sci-MMR exposes substantial gaps in acquiring and integrating evidence, underscoring the need for truly explainable, evidence-grounded scientific reasoning benchmarks.

title: SEED-UMI: Sharing the Exoskeleton between human and robot for onE-to-one Dexterous demonstration
summary: Imitation learning for dexterous hands is bottlenecked by the difficulty of collecting contact-rich demonstrations that transfer faithfully to the robot. Prior wearable-exoskeleton systems record only on the human side and retarget via open-loop mappings calibrated in free space, which degrade under contact. We present SEED-UMI, a framework in which both the human and the robot wear the same exoskeleton: joint encoders become a physically shared measurement, and wrist cameras mounted to the exoskeleton observe the same outer mechanism during both human data collection and robot policy rollouts. This turns retargeting into paired cross-embodiment supervision and lets policies train directly on raw exoskeleton-centric wrist images, without segmentation or inpainting. On five contact-rich tasks, SEED-UMI achieves 3.0x greater data collection efficiency than exoskeleton-based teleoperation and a 70.0% average rollout success rate.

AI.tldr: SEED-UMI aligns human and robot through a shared exoskeleton, using joint encoders and wrist cameras to enable paired cross-embodiment supervision and training on raw exoskeleton-centric wrist images, improving data efficiency and success in contact-rich imitation learning.
AI.motivation: Address the data bottleneck in imitation learning for dexterous hands by eliminating fragile open-loop retargeting and enabling direct learning from aligned, exoskeleton-centric observations, especially under contact.
AI.method: Both human and robot wear the same exoskeleton; joint encoders provide a physically shared state; wrist cameras capture the same outer mechanism during data collection and policy execution; training uses raw wrist images without segmentation or inpainting; cross-embodiment supervision replaces retargeting.
AI.result: 3.0x higher data collection efficiency than exoskeleton-based teleoperation; average rollout success rate of 70% across five contact-rich tasks.
AI.conclusion: Cross-embodiment supervision with a shared exoskeleton enables data-efficient, faithful imitation learning for dexterous manipulation under contact, reducing retargeting errors and bypassing image segmentation requirements.

title: HERALD: High-Fidelity Exemplar Retrieval with Adaptive Landmark Distillation for Heterophily-Aware Graph Condensation
summary: Graph condensation aims to produce a small surrogate graph that preserves the downstream node-classification performance of a much larger original graph. Existing methods rely on Weisfeiler-Lehman neighbourhood aggregation or gradient-based distribution matching, both of which assume that adjacent nodes share the same label, an assumption that breaks down under heterophily. We propose HERALD (High-fidelity Exemplar Retrieval with Adaptive Landmark Distillation), a gradient-free graph condensation framework that adapts the node scoring and feature selection in the condensation pipeline to the graph's measured heterophily. HERALD selects features via a joint Fisher-discriminability and activation-density criterion that down-weights aggregated representations on heterophilic graphs, and scores nodes by a weighted combination of prototype representativeness, decision-boundary proximity, and Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID), where the weights are driven by a smooth sigmoid function of the heterophily ratio. Nodes are then assembled into a condensed subgraph through score-ordered BFS expansion, Personalised PageRank pruning, and class rebalancing, all at an identical storage budget to BONSAI, enabling direct comparison. Experiments on eight benchmark datasets spanning homophilic and heterophilic settings show that HERALD matches or outperforms state-of-the-art condensers on heterophilic graphs and remains competitive on homophilic ones across four GNN architectures.

AI.tldr: HERALD is a gradient-free graph condenser that adapts to heterophily, using a joint discriminability-activation criterion for features and a heterophily-informed scoring of nodes to assemble a compact graph that preserves downstream classification.
AI.motivation: Existing graph condensers rely on WL neighbourhood aggregation or gradient-based distribution matching, which assume label consistency among adjacent nodes. This assumption fails under heterophily, necessitating a gradient-free, heterophily-aware condensation method.
AI.method: HERALD selects features via a joint Fisher-discriminability and activation-density criterion that down-weights aggregated representations on heterophilic graphs. Nodes are scored by a weighted mix of prototype representativeness, decision-boundary proximity, and Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID), with weights driven by a sigmoid function of the measured heterophily ratio. The condensed subgraph is built via score-ordered BFS expansion, Personalized PageRank pruning, and class rebalancing, all under the same storage budget as BONSAI.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on eight benchmark datasets spanning homophilic and heterophilic settings shows that HERALD matches or surpasses state-of-the-art condensers on heterophilic graphs and remains competitive on homophilic graphs across four GNN architectures.
AI.conclusion: HERALD provides a robust, gradient-free condensation framework that adaptively accounts for heterophily, achieving high fidelity node-classification performance with a fixed storage budget and strong performance across both heterophilic and homophilic graphs.

title: From Evaluation to Enhancement: Benchmarking and Improving Think-with-Video Reasoning for Video Generative Models
summary: Video generation has advanced to produce visually compelling and temporally coherent results. Yet, whether these models can genuinely think with video--executing symbolic rules, respecting physical laws, and pursuing intentional goals--remains an open question. Existing benchmarks only partially address this, often conflating visual quality with cognitive correctness. We introduce VWG-Bench (Video World Generalist Benchmark), a comprehensive benchmark spanning 9 reasoning dimensions and 38 fine-grained tasks. To enable precise diagnosis, we design a three-level VLM-as-Judge protocol that independently assesses video-level fluency, task-level rule adherence, and sample-level goal realization. Evaluations of leading models reveal a striking gap: while models achieve strong rendering scores, they consistently fail on logic-heavy and rule-constrained tasks. To address this, we propose Vid-PRE (Video Prompt Reasoner and Enhancer), a model-agnostic prompt rewriter that offloads the cognitive burden of reasoning to a dedicated VLM. Trained via reinforcement learning with purely text-based rewards, Vid-PRE produces concise, constraint-aware prompts without the instability of video-level reward signals. Experiments show that Vid-PRE yields substantial reasoning improvements across multiple generators without architectural modifications. Together, VWG-Bench and Vid-PRE offer a rigorous diagnostic lens and a scalable path toward true think-with-video capabilities. All data and code are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/KlingTeam/VWG-Bench.

AI.tldr: VWG-Bench offers a 9-dimension, 38-task diagnostic suite for video reasoning, using a three-level VLM-as-Judge to separate fluency, rule adherence, and goal realization; Vid-PRE is a prompt rewriter using text-based RL rewards to boost reasoning without changing architectures, improving performance across generators.
AI.motivation: To rigorously diagnose think-with-video capabilities by decoupling visual rendering quality from cognitive compliance with rules and goals, addressing gaps in existing benchmarks.
AI.method: VWG-Bench employs 38 fine-grained tasks across 9 reasoning dimensions and a three-level VLM-as-Judge protocol (video-level fluency, task-level rule adherence, sample-level goal realization). Vid-PRE is a model-agnostic prompt rewriter trained with reinforcement learning using text-based rewards to produce constraint-aware prompts for video generators.
AI.result: Leading video models maintain strong rendering scores but underperform on logic-heavy, rule-constrained tasks. Vid-PRE yields substantial reasoning improvements across multiple generators without architectural changes.
AI.conclusion: VWG-Bench provides a rigorous diagnostic framework; Vid-PRE offers a scalable, architecture-agnostic path to improve think-with-video capabilities via better prompting; dataset and code are publicly available.

title: AI-Powered Flare Combustion Efficiency Estimation
comment: Accepted at the 4th International Conference on Machine Learning and Data Engineering (ICMLDE 2025). 5 pages
summary: Achieving high combustion efficiency in flare stacks is crucial for adhering to regulatory standards and controlling the release of hydrocarbons into the environment. Traditional instruments like gas analyzers and hyperspectral cameras are expensive, fragile, and require frequent calibration, which makes them impractical for remote or budget constrained industrial sites. We propose an innovative solution that combines a lightweight vision-language encoder with a compact multi-layer perceptron to predict combustion efficiency directly from low-cost thermal video footage. The fully trained model is integrated into an easy-to-deploy graphical user interface. This interface overlays predicted combustion efficiency values on each video frame, displays real-time trends in combustion efficiency, shows the distribution of combustion efficiency across all frames in the video, and allows users to export CSV reports. Over a six-month period, the system achieved 99% uptime and required less than 15 minutes of maintenance per week.

AI.tldr: Low-cost, vision-based system predicts flare-stack combustion efficiency from thermal video using a vision-language encoder and a compact MLP, with a deployable GUI for per-frame values, real-time trends, distributions, and CSV reporting.
AI.motivation: Reduce reliance on expensive gas analyzers and hyperspectral cameras, enabling accurate combustion efficiency monitoring on remote or budget-constrained sites while supporting regulatory compliance and environmental protections.
AI.method: Leverages a lightweight vision-language encoder combined with a compact multi-layer perceptron to estimate combustion efficiency directly from low-cost thermal video. The trained model is embedded in a graphical user interface that overlays per-frame predictions, shows real-time trends and frame distributions, and allows CSV export.
AI.result: Achieved 99% system uptime over six months with maintenance requirements under 15 minutes per week.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates a practical, cost-effective, and robust solution for real-time combustion efficiency monitoring suitable for resource-limited industrial settings, potentially broadening access to regulatory-compliant flare monitoring.

title: Visual-SLAM for the detection of hidden tomatoes in greenhouses by Hierarchical Localization and GLOMAPfor robotized harvesting
summary: Advanced crop monitoring inside greenhouses is becoming one of the primary objectives of research centers. High-performance sensors, such as LiDAR or stereo cameras, have traditionally been employed for this purpose, though these often have a high cost. This work proposes a Visual-SLAM system using a monocular camera, which is significantly more cost-effective and specifically tailored for agricultural applications, such as mapping tomato crops in a greenhouse. Tests were carried out on a real tomato bunch, located in the Agroconnect experimental greenhouse. A ROS 2 Humble node was developed to run on the robot in order to capture images of these crops, which were then stored for offline processing. To generate a 3D mapped model for the crop in the greenhouse, the GLOMAP mapper, based on Structure-From-Motion, was integrated with the Hierarchical Localization toolbox. This initial mapping is a foundation for future, more advanced algorithms to analyze growth patterns, and optimize agricultural management. The system leverages a hierarchical localization paradigm based on a coarse-to-fine strategy: it first performs global retrieval to generate location hypotheses, then combines local features within the identified candidate regions.
